metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is predominantly negative (-1.00) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast upward; correct by reducing forecast peak values, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias in next 5-7 days, especially if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., +1.00 after 3+ consecutive -1.00), model often overreacts with excessive upward momentum; cap forecast growth to 5-8% above prior 10-day moving avg.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed; reduce forecast tail (last 5-7 days) by 3-5% relative to 10-day moving avg.
- When sentiment is positive but recent price action is flat or declining, model tends to over-forecast upward; apply downward correction to 10-15 day horizon, especially if sentiment is weak or inconsistent.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in first 5 days of horizon, apply “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 1-2% per day until price stabilizes or sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70% of 30-day moving avg, model often over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 5-10% for next 10 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.
